title: Review --- Three Jobs, No New Words

lessons.title: Review — three jobs, no new words
lessons.gloss: review — a whole grammatical machine assembled from two words you already had

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Nothing new. One question first: how many new words did this rung teach you?
None. Here is the whole rung:

utterances: joining to a noun. Spanish: el libro que compro. English: the book that I buy.
the same, with English's that dropped. Spanish: la casa que tengo. English: the house I have.
no noun to join to. Spanish: lo que digo. English: what I say.

segments.text: Que you have held since quiero que hables. Lo you have held since the object pronouns. This rung put them to work and added nothing.

That is worth pausing on, because it is the last big structural piece a beginner's course owes you, and it turned out to cost no vocabulary at all. Almost everything in a language is like this eventually: the pieces stop being new and start being rearranged.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: what to actually watch for

segments.text: One error will outlive the others, so it gets the last word here.
English deletes its joint. Spanish never does.
You will think the book I bought, translate what you thought, and produce el libro compré. It will feel complete because your English was complete.
The check is mechanical and takes a second: a noun, then a new subject and verb, with nothing in between — that gap needs a que.
And when there is no noun to begin with, lo supplies one so that que has something to hang from. Which means both chapters were about the same thing: Spanish will not let the joint go missing.

segments.instruction: all three rows of the table
segments.source: [YOU SAY: all three rows of the table]

segments.text: Until the missing English that is loud.

segments.prompt: How many new words did this rung introduce?

feedback.correct: Que and lo were both already yours.

segments.prompt: Say the house I have, and name the trap.
acceptedResponses: la casa que tengo; english drops the that

feedback.correct: You think the English, and the que goes missing with it.
feedback.incorrect: La casa que tengo. The trap is that English deletes its that.

segments.prompt: When there is no noun to join to, what supplies one?

feedback.correct: So that que has something to hang from.
feedback.incorrect: Lo — giving que something to attach to.

segments.text: New words this rung? (None.) The error that outlives the others? (Dropping que, because English drops that.) Next: sentences long enough to be worth saying.
